title: Will Oil Prices Decline as Middle East Supply Recovers? - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Oil prices are expected to moderate over the next year as supply from the Middle East gradually recovers, according to Goldman Sachs Research. However, high prices may last longer than anticipated given the risk of renewed escalation in the conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran. A barrel of benchmark Brent crude oil is expected to trade at $90 in December 2026, a slight increase from a recent forecast of $85, according to Daan Struyven, co-head of global commodities research and head of oil research. Struyven predicts the Brent price will average $80 a barrel in 2027. “We maintain our base case that continued adaptation of Middle East supply will eventually reduce crude oil prices, while potential renewed escalation still poses significant net upside risk,” Struyven and his team write in a report. The supply of oil from the Middle East declined after the outbreak of the conflict, but exporters have adapted faster than expected. Our researchers estimate that Persian Gulf oil exports have rebounded and have been around their 2025 average since late September. That calculation includes an estimated four million barrels per day (mb/d) of “dark” exports—shipments on tankers that keep their transponders turned off to hide their movements. Given the recovery in exports from the Middle East, why is the price of oil still so high? A barrel of dated Brent crude scheduled for delivery in the next month is trading at more than $130, while benchmark Brent futures have recently been above $100. “Physical prices remain elevated because escalation threatens supply while near-record-low global inventories fuel strong restocking demand,” Struyven writes. For example, Iran or the Houthis could target oil infrastructure in the region, including ports, pipelines, and oil fields. Struyven estimates that spot prices for Brent crude include a nearly $25 risk premium on top of their fair value because supply could be curtailed and inventories could be drawn down further if there is an escalation. At the same time, the sensitivity of global stocks and bonds to oil prices has created increasing demand for oil as a hedge for portfolios. This is another factor helping keep prices high. Helping to keep prices in check, on the other hand, is the base case expectation that the balance between supply and demand in the global market for crude oil and other liquid fuels will shift to a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026 and in 2027, the researchers find. Struyven describes this as “the key driver” of his team’s forecast for crude prices to moderate. In fact, the oil market was nearly balanced in September. Goldman Sachs Research estimates that demand exceeded supply by just 0.3 mb/d that month, a dramatic easing from the 7.2 mb/d supply deficit in March. The market’s return to balance is likely the result of higher non-Gulf oil production and a decline in global oil demand, offsetting the remaining deficit in production from the Persian Gulf. Also, the crude oil market was operating with a surplus in 2025. Global demand for oil declined by roughly 1.3 mb/d in September 2026 compared with the 2025 average as oil prices climbed, Struyven writes. The recovery of Persian Gulf oil shipments, as producers adapt to the conflict there, also supports the base case that the oil market will soon be back in balance, Struyven writes. His team expects the supply of oil from the Persian Gulf to “trend higher as continued adaptation and added transportation resources—especially pipelines and a larger tanker fleet—support further gains,” he adds. Finally, our commodities analysts say that the shock to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz is likely to continue to weigh on the global demand for oil, bringing the market nearer to balance. Oil demand in the third quarter of 2026 was down by 3.3 mb/d year-over-year, “with much of the weakness concentrated in China, the Middle East, and OECD Asia,” Struyven writes. Our analysts estimate that global oil demand in the third quarter was nearly 4 mb/d below its hypothetical path if there had been no oil shock from the war in Iran. They assume that 80% of this gap between actual global demand and the counterfactual will unwind by the fourth quarter of 2027, with the dropoff in demand narrowing to 0.7 mb/d as the availability and affordability of refined oil products gradually improve. “This forecast that oil demand largely recovers is directionally consistent with the demand recovery from prior negative oil supply shocks in 2011 and 2022, and our view that the weakness in Chinese petrochemicals oil demand is largely unsustainable,” Struyven writes. Still, the expected 0.7 mb/d hit to global oil demand that is forecast for the fourth quarter of 2027 reflects the team’s finding that the oil shock has accelerated behavioral changes, especially in the use of existing electric vehicles and trucks in China instead of oil-based equivalents and in electric vehicle sales. title: Birdie G’s Resurrects With a ‘70s-Drenched Dining Room and the Beloved Pickle Chick - Eater Los Angeles
content: The Midwest and Jewish–inflected restaurant will open at Fairmont Century Plaza on October 26 Jeremy Fox’s beloved Santa Monica restaurant, Birdie G’s, will resurrect at Fairmont Century Plaza after closing at the end of 2025. Named after Fox’s daughter Birdie and grandmother Gladys, the restaurant will reopen on October 26, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner with a mix of original favorites, such as the Pickle Chick, and new dishes, including a Rancho Gordo bean–based poached egg ribollita. When Fox first spoke with Fairmont Century Plaza about Birdie’s G’s in June 2025, it was supposed to be the restaurant’s second location. But as it became increasingly clear that the Bergamot Station Arts Center outpost could not remain open, nothing was set in stone; at the time of the closure, Fox believed Birdie G’s might be gone for good. “In life, you very rarely get second chances, and in a restaurant even less so,” he says. “So I feel very fortunate and grateful that I didn’t have to tell Birdie that her restaurant was done.” Add Eater as a preferred source to see more of our reporting on Google. While the original Birdie G’s served only dinner, the Century City location will open at 6 a.m. for coffee, with its Midwest and Jewish–inflected breakfast and lunch available from 6:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and dinner from 5:30 to 9:30 p.m. The breakfast menu opens with Birdie’s muesli crowned with banana and apple, along with a cornbread waffle paired with sweet pepper jam, citrusy blood orange agrumato-dressed avocado toast, a build-your-own omelet, koji-marinated steak and eggs, and a smoked fish platter. Lunch brings a corned beef Reuben on Bub & Grandma’s bread, rice flour–batter mushroom fritto misto, the return of the famed gluten-free pickle chicken, three sizes of steak frites spanning eight to 28 ounces, and cauliflower kugel. The dinner menu, which offers many of the same dishes as lunch, sees the return of the Hangtown Brei with fried oyster and pork belly that Fox describes as “very decadent, over-the-top, semi-blasphemous,” lamb à la sales, and the stained-glass-like rose petal pie, plus new options such as rotisserie chicken and vegetables. “I like to refer to it as bubbe cuisine,” Fox says. “Just trying to channel that kind of no-nonsense, bare-bones, straight-to-the-point cooking.” The restaurant will also bring back some of Birdie G’s former staff, including bar director Stephanie Redding, who will consult on the drinks; Laura Eldrige, who will work in the bar; and former cooks. Over the years, Fox and the Birdie G’s team documented most of their recipes, which will be the basis for the new location. Birdie G’s in Santa Monica is the first restaurant Fox designed from the ground up; looking back, he says he didn’t quite understand the process or know how to advocate for his ideas at the time. “It was a really cool warehouse space, but nothing about it tied into the concept, the vibe, the atmosphere, to what I wanted Birdie G’s to be,” Fox says. In Century City, he collaborated with EDG Design to help bring his initial vision to fruition. The restaurant stands in stark contrast to the rest of the upscale hotel, bathed in neutral stone and punctuated by indoor greenery. Strong 1970s inspiration permeates the dining room, from the burnt-mustard banquettes to the plaid bar stools and repeating triangular wallpaper that looks like it could be found in a retro basement. Artwork shaped into small galleries adorns the walls, including vintage magazine covers like a 1987 Sports Illustrated issue featuring Joe Carter and Corey Snyder of the Cleveland Indians (now Guardians), and a painting of two birds in dinner coats. “It definitely feels like you’re somewhere else in time, somewhere else in the country,” Fox says. For Fox, Birdie G’s was never meant to be a hotspot. Instead, he hoped the restaurant would feel like it had been there forever; it was initially inspired by his love of chain restaurants like Applebee’s and the Cheesecake Factory. Fox points to 1996’s Big Night as something that influenced him to go to culinary school at all. While he worked in fine dining at restaurants including Rustic Canyon, he kept returning to the cozy Italian restaurant run by the brothers in Big Night as a reference for what he hoped to do. “I wanted that restaurant that was simple, that was earnest, that wasn’t trendy,” Fox says. Decades into Fox’s career, the Century City Birdie G’s feels like something entirely new for him. He says that over the last five years, as he and the industry faced numerous difficulties, it’s been hard to operate as a confident creative force. When Birdie G’s closed in Santa Monica, he suddenly faced, for the first time in many years, not having somewhere to report to every day. Now, as he prepares to reopen Birdie G’s and continues developing his San Luis Obispo restaurant, Edna, he’s feeling hopeful about what is next. “This is me really needing a W,” Fox says. “Really needing a win.” Reservations for Birdie G’s are available on OpenTable. title: GS Caltex Advances With Four Double-Digit Scores - 조선일보
content: Hyundai Engineering & Construction, without Yang Hyo-jin, exits group stage without a set win [OSEN=Cho Hyung-rae Reporter] GS Caltex, the V-League championship playoff winner from last season, advanced to the semifinals of the cup tournament. Hyundai Engineering & Construction concluded the tournament without winning a single set. GS Caltex secured a decisive 3-0 (25-23, 25-15, 25-22) victory in the second round of Group B in the women’s division of the 2026 Yeosu-NH Nonghyup Cup Professional Volleyball Tournament against Hyundai Engineering & Construction, held at the Jinnam Gymnasium in Yeosu on October 16. With this, GS Caltex marked a 1-1 record and advanced to the semifinals. Hyundai Engineering & Construction, with two losses, was eliminated in the group stage. In their first tournament without retired Yang Hyo-jin, Hyundai Engineering & Construction failed to win a single set. GS Caltex saw Silva score 17 points, Tanacha 13, Kwon Minji 11, and Choi Ga-eun 10. Four players scored double-digit points, showcasing balanced performance. Choi Ga-eun dominated the center with seven successful blocks, supported by Oh Se-yeon’s three blocks. Silva, Kwon Minji, and Oh Se-yeon each contributed two serve points. The first set was tightly contested, with Hyundai Engineering & Construction initially seizing control. After a 5-5 tie, Jordan’s back attack and Lee Ye-rim’s quick open attack gave them momentum. Mega’s consecutive points and Lee Ye-rim’s quick open attack extended their lead to 11-7. However, GS Caltex tied the score at 11-11 with Oh Se-yeon’s quick attack, Silva’s open attack, Kwon Minji’s block, and open attack. Oh Se-yeon’s quick attack, an opponent’s attack error, Silva’s block, and open attack helped GS Caltex take a 16-12 lead. Hyundai Engineering & Construction narrowed the gap with Mega’s open attack and Jordan’s block points. But GS Caltex secured the first set with Kwon Minji and Tanacha’s quick open attacks, Silva’s back attack, and Oh Se-yeon’s block and direct open attack. Hyundai Engineering & Construction rallied with Kim Hee-jin’s quick open attack and Bae Yu-na and Jordan’s block points, but Silva ultimately clinched the first set. The second set tilted early in GS Caltex’s favor. Kwon Minji’s open attack and serve points, Silva’s back attack, and Choi Ga-eun’s consecutive blocks gave them an 11-3 lead. Kwon Minji’s serve alone earned eight points. Hyundai Engineering & Construction countered with Kim Hee-jin’s quick attack and blocks, but it was insufficient. GS Caltex expanded their lead with Silva’s open attack, Oh Se-yeon and Silva’s serve points, and Choi Ga-eun’s blocks, winning the second set by a large margin. In the third set, Hyundai Engineering & Construction took a 14-10 lead after Mega’s open attack and Kim Hee-jin’s serve points at 10-10. GS Caltex chased with points from Kwon Minji, Lee Ju-ah, and Tanacha. Hyundai Engineering & Construction resisted with Mega’s consecutive back attack points. GS Caltex narrowed the gap with Kim Ji-won’s serve points. The match remained tense as the star players Mega and Silva traded blows, but Mega’s error and Oh Se-yeon’s serve point made it 23-21. Choi Ga-eun’s block set up the match point, and Kwon Minji’s open attack sealed the victory.

title: Best Bikes For Comfortable Couple Touring And Solo Adventures - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update Finding one motorcycle that genuinely works for both solo weekend blasts and two-up touring is harder than it sounds — but it's far from impossible. Managing two bikes means doubling up on maintenance, storage, and cost, and somewhere in that equation your riding time (and your partner's patience) starts to suffer. The good news is that today's market offers a remarkable range of machines that handle both roles without meaningful compromise. You don't have to sacrifice performance for pillion comfort, or vice versa. You just need to pick the right bike for both duties. Given how far modern motorcycles have come, that's an easier task than ever — there are even full-dress tourers now that can get down and dirty in corners. Here are 10 motorcycles that excel at solo adventures just as much as two-up tours. In the sub-500cc adventure segment, there's hardly anything more balanced than the Himalayan 450, to the point where it might make you wonder why you'd ever need anything else. When you want to have fun, you can take it off-roading and exploit everything that Harris Performance's chassis and suspension have to offer. When the mood strikes to tour, add your bags and the Himalayan 450 is good to go for miles. The Sherpa engine has more than enough pep to keep up with highway speeds, while the long-travel suspension keeps things planted on rougher surfaces. The Super Meteor 650 offers an impressive cruiser package, powered by a smooth parallel-twin engine that delivers refined, linear power with ample low- to mid-range torque. It feels calm and relaxed at highway speeds, even with a pillion on board. The bike adds to that with neutral handling and relaxed ergonomics. For touring, the Celestial trim adds a windscreen to keep the wind off your chest and a pillion backrest for added support. It also carries a proper big-bike road presence, so there's no shortage of space for saddlebags. It's a terrific cruiser that can handle both long tours and weekend rides up a mountain. If an identity crisis came with two wheels, it would be the Kawasaki Versys 650. It sits somewhere between an adventure tourer and a sport tourer, but that's actually a strength — it can be whatever you need it to be. The Ninja 650-derived engine and 17-inch wheels let you have fun in the corners, while the tall windscreen, relaxed ergonomics, and generously sized seats make it excellent on the highway. Long-travel suspension means rough roads don't require a gear change. It will never blow your mind, but it will take you and your pillion wherever you want to go without complaint. If you want something like the Versys 650 in a sportier package, look toward the Tiger Sport 800. What makes this bike stand out is its inline-triple engine, celebrated for its versatile character — strong mid-range torque paired with a rewarding top-end pull. Compared to the Tiger Sport 660, this 800 also gains 33 more horsepower and an upgraded suspension. Cruise control and a bidirectional quickshifter round out the package nicely. Bear in mind that, while you can certainly do a two-up tour on this bike, it leans slightly more toward the sporty side. The Suzuki GSX-S1000GT+ is one of the finest sport tourers currently on sale. It undercuts most of its competition while delivering a surprising level of both comfort and performance. It draws its inline-four engine from the GSX-R superbike, putting 150 horsepower at your disposal. Suzuki also carries over the superbike-derived frame, which handles corners with confidence. Meanwhile, the suspension and bodywork are engineered for the long haul — a large windscreen up front, standard side cases, and wide, well-padded seats. This is perhaps the closest you can get to a dedicated touring bike without giving up sporty performance. The Africa Twin Adventure Sports ES is a more road-biased version of the standard model. While it trades a degree of off-road capability for on-road comfort, the swap is well worth it for touring riders. Much of the credit goes to its Showa EERA semi-active suspension, which adapts to road surfaces on the fly, keeping the bike composed at all times — even with a pillion aboard. The overall package is made even more compelling by its sub-$18,000 price point. Simply put, the Adventure Sports ES is a complete globe-trotting machine without the globe-trotting price tag. Since its inception, the BMW GS line has set the benchmark for the adventure segment, and the R 1300 GS continues that tradition. This is the most refined GS yet, equally at home on a gravel track or a sweeping motorway. It retains the iconic boxer-twin architecture — valued for its versatility and long-term reliability — with ample power for sustained highway miles. The EVO Telelever/Paralever suspension system works in concert to deliver comfort across all surfaces, and the optional DSA electronic suspension raises that bar further. And if you think it can't handle a bit of mountain fun, Greg Mansell would like to have a word with you. No conversation about two-up touring is complete without the granddaddy of touring motorcycles: the Gold Wing Tour. This legendary machine offers everything you'd ever want from a touring bike — a butter-smooth flat-six engine, couch-like comfort for rider and pillion alike, and generous storage throughout. It builds on that foundation with electronic suspension, Walking Mode, cruise control, a full infotainment system, and more. Remarkably, Honda positions this as a performance-first tourer capable of handling corners and spirited riding, thanks to its double-wishbone front suspension, low center of gravity, and optimized chassis geometry. It's a business-class experience that makes the near-$30,000 price tag look like genuine value. Spend over $35,000, and you enter the serious American touring category, where few full-dressers rival the Pursuit Dark Horse. It is powered by a 126-horsepower Powerplus 112 V-twin engine, making highway cruising feel effortless. Ergonomically, the scooped saddle provides solid support for the rider, while the massive top case doubles as a backrest throne for your pillion. A substantial fairing adds meaningful wind protection for both occupants. Look deeper, and you'll find a comprehensive feature set: a large TFT display, an optional 100-watt PowerBand audio system, numerous rider aids, over 36 gallons of storage, and Brembo brakes. While this Indian has the power to have some fun on the road, you do trade a sporty character for your pillion's comfort. If you want a comfortable American tourer without sacrificing performance, the CVO Street Glide belongs at the top of your list. This is one of the most luxurious Harley-Davidson motorcycles ever produced, blending timeless bagger style with premium features and modern technology. Power comes from a Milwaukee-Eight 121 VVT engine, delivering commanding output for both highway cruising and spirited riding. Harley also claims the suspension is plush on the open road while remaining confidence-inspiring in the corners. It builds on that with a 12.3-inch TFT display, a powerful Rockford Fosgate audio system, and cornering-enabled rider aids. The custom styling is simply unmissable on the road. While $50,000 is a significant investment, this is about as high-performing as a full-dress tourer gets without compromising pillion comfort. You may still want to add a pillion backrest, but that's spare change relative to the bike's price tag. We want to hear from you. title: Lawson launches custom guitar ahead of the US GP - The Race
content: F1 driver by day, musician by… Thursday evening? Liam Lawson will make his debut in VCARB's Garage Sessions music and culture event ahead of the United States Grand Prix at Austin, while launching his very own custom Taylor Guitars LL30 GS Mini Special Edition. The guitar features a pink to white ombre design, and his racing number 30 in the centre. Liam has loved music since his childhood, as his Dad encouraged him and his brother to play from the age of six. Not quite the career path Liam ended up taking, though. The event kicks off on Thursday at Inn Cahoots on Austin’s East 6th Street, with the Esses Bazaar from 3pm, featuring live music, food, western wear, glam stations, tattoos and a chance to get up close and grab a photo with the team’s show car. Garage Sessions follows at 7pm, where Liam will perform live next to his former childhood bandmates, including his brother and two close friends! The wider line up features a mix of emerging talent and established songwriters like Jonathan Capeci, Scoot Teasley, Jess Farren, Alison Nichols, and Drake Milligan. Liam said: “I feel very proud to be launching my partnership with Taylor Guitars at Garage Sessions. Playing the guitar has been a big part of my life since I was young, as my Dad played in a band throughout my childhood. He encouraged my brother and I to play since we were six years old, so it feels like a full circle moment to be launching a custom LL30 GS Mini SE while performing with my brother and two friends who I grew up playing with. "Music is a big part of my life, and I use it to clear my head during the season, so I'm really excited to perform at Garage Sessions where we can connect with fans outside of the track. I’m look ing forward to meeting everyone there.” With Garage Sessions bringing together racing, music, and community, Racing Bulls is giving fans another reason to get excited about Austin, and giving Lawson a chance to show off a skill that doesn’t involve a steering wheel. title: German Exports Rebound amid Demand from the US, EU, and AI Buildout - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Germany’s exports increased in the first half of 2026 and are providing a modest boost to GDP growth in Europe’s largest economy, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Our economists forecast that real exports will grow at a “robust” rate of 3.5% in 2026 and 2.4% the following year. Recent export strength reflects resilient foreign demand alongside modest, productivity-driven improvements in competitiveness. Goldman Sachs Research expects German exports to increase, driven by revived trade with the US and the European Union, plus the global artificial intelligence (AI) buildout. “Taken together, we are more optimistic about German export performance than at the start of 2026,” writes Niklas Garnadt, an economist in Goldman Sachs Research, in a report. Strong export performance in the first half of 2026 is consistent with healthy foreign demand and a modest improvement in relative unit labor costs, driven by stronger productivity growth. Garnadt cautions that competition from Chinese exporters is expected to continue weighing on German exports in the medium term, especially in third markets. Still, the brighter outlook marks a shift for a sector that has been a drag on growth since the onset of the European energy crisis in 2022, writes Garnadt. Increases in relative unit labor costs and the real effective exchange rate have recently taken a toll on German competitiveness. The near-term outlook for exports has “improved materially,” Garnadt writes. Survey-based, forward-looking export indicators have risen to their highest levels since the start of the European energy crisis. Hard data show that foreign manufacturing sales have risen since the start of the year, alongside a recovery in real goods exports. Foreign orders have increased even more sharply. This suggests further export growth in the quarters to come, according to Goldman Sachs Research. In addition to improved competitiveness, German exports to the US are recovering from the decline triggered last year by US tariffs. While exports in the second quarter remained materially below pre-tariff levels, the shortfall peaked in the second half of 2025 and has narrowed since then, writes Garnadt. Recent monthly economic data point to further improvement in the third quarter. Trade with the EU is also rebounding after the slump that followed the energy crunch four years ago. “Since early 2025, EU trade has become a significant tailwind, reflected in rising manufacturing sales and orders,” writes Garnadt. Thanks to the development of AI infrastructure worldwide, German computer, electronics, and electrical equipment companies are making meaningful contributions to export growth. AI-exposed goods have materially outperformed total exported goods over the past year, according to Goldman Sachs Research There was also stronger growth in exports of chemicals and intermediate goods in the first half of 2026, perhaps reflecting precautionary purchases related to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz this year. Garnadt writes that this trend may partly reverse in the months to come. And Chinese competition will remain a challenge over the medium term. Even so, Garnadt points out that Germany’s surprisingly positive performance in the first half of 2026 shows a significant shift in the export sector following a long period of relative weakness. “Positive near-term indicators, productivity-driven competitiveness gains, stronger demand from Europe and the US, and spillovers from the global AI cycle point to healthy export growth ahead,” he writes. title: BMW Motorrad Presents the New BMW F 450 RR. - BMW Group
content:
Juliane DreslerBMW Group
            

            Tel: +49-151-601-95733



              send an e-mail “What I particularly like about the new BMW F 450 RR is how
    light, direct, and precise it is to ride. To me, that’s exactly what
    a supersport motorcycle should be. It’s great fun on twisty roads
    and performs just as well on the racetrack. At the same time, it
    clearly carries the DNA of our RR models. For me, it’s the perfect
    entry into the world of BMW RR motorcycles.”
Markus Flasch, CEO BMW Motorrad The new BMW F 450 RR: A lightweight supersport bike for the 
48-hp class—developed for precise handling and an immediate
    racing feel on winding country roads and the racetrack.
The new BMW F 450 RR for the 48-hp class was developed as a
  standalone supersport bike within the BMW F 450 model family. The
  focus was on signature BMW riding pleasure, enabled by
  supersport-specific chassis and geometry engineering, rigorous weight
  optimization, and a powerful parallel-twin engine. Its design clearly
  follows the current design language of the S 1000 RR and visually
  underscores its dynamic ambitions. The silhouette consistently translates this ambition into RR design
  language: the pronounced nose-down, tail-up stance, the signature
  RR flyline, and the winglets create a powerful forward orientation.
  Asymmetrical side fairing panels, gills on the right side, and the
  split face add distinctive accents and underscore the standalone
  interpretation of RR DNA. The LED headlight with its
  signature RR daytime running light design defines the bike’s
  distinctive appearance. Smooth and characterful parallel-twin engine with a 135-degree
    crankpin offset for dynamic riding pleasure.
At the heart of the new BMW F 450 RR is the newly developed
  fuel-injected parallel-twin engine first used in the F 450 GS,
  together with a stainless-steel underfloor muffler. For use in the
  F 450 RR, it has been specifically tuned to meet the requirements of a
  supersport bike and gives the motorcycle a particularly distinctive
  sound. With an output of 35 kW (48 hp) at 8,750 rpm and maximum torque
  of 43 Nm at 6,750 rpm, the new F 450 RR delivers powerful acceleration
  and confident roll-on performance. As much as 80 percent of the
  available torque is already on tap at 3,000 rpm, providing strong
  propulsion from low engine speeds. High-tech materials and optimized
  internal friction make these performance figures possible from exactly
  420 cc. This makes the engine one of the most compact and powerful
  units in the A2 parallel-twin segment. It not only meets the stringent
  Euro 5+ requirements, but is also particularly efficient, with fuel
  consumption of just 3.8 liters per 100 km. With its 14-liter fuel
  tank, the F 450 RR achieves a range of more than 350 km. The service
  interval is the BMW Motorrad-standard 10,000 km. The crankshaft with a 135-degree crankpin offset and a balance shaft
  combine characterful power delivery with excellent refinement and low
  vibration. Magnesium covers for the clutch and transmission support
  weight optimization. Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) for a significant increase in operating
    and riding comfort.
The optional Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) engages the clutch
  according to engine speed, increasing comfort and control—especially
  in urban traffic, while maneuvering, on winding country roads, and
  during sporty riding. In combination with Shift Assistant Pro, it
  enables riding and shifting without manual clutch operation; the
  clutch lever remains available for deliberate rider input. For the BMW F 450 RR M Sport, the ERC is available ex-factory as part
  of the Innovation Package; it can be retrofitted to all other variants
  as an Original BMW Motorrad Accessory. During overrun, the clutch
  remains closed, preserving engine braking until shortly before the
  motorcycle comes to a stop. Only when idle speed is reached does the
  ERC open automatically, reliably preventing the engine from stalling. Six-speed transmission and left-side secondary drive. Shift
    Assistant Pro for fast upshifts and downshifts without operating the
      clutch.
The six-speed transmission transfers torque to the left-side
  secondary drive via an X-ring chain. For rapid upshifts and downshifts
  without operating the clutch, the new F 450 RR is equipped with Shift
  Assistant Pro in every equipment variant except the base model. It can
  be retrofitted to the base model. ABS Pro, DBC, DTC, and MSR, plus the “Rain,” “Road,” and
    “Race” riding modes as standard—delivering a high level of riding
    pleasure and safety.
The standard “Rain,” “Road,” and “Race” riding modes allow
  riders to tailor the new BMW F 450 RR to their
  individual preferences. ABS Pro, Dynamic Brake Control (DBC), Dynamic
  Traction Control (DTC), and engine drag torque control (MSR) are also standard. Chassis with a tubular steel space frame for high rigidity,
    robustness, and riding precision. Supersport-specific tuning and a
    short wheelbase for agile handling and high stability.
The new BMW F 450 RR also uses the newly developed
  BMW F 450 GS chassis concept as its technical foundation, with a setup
  tailored specifically to supersport use. The tuning focused on agile
  handling, precise feedback, and high stability on winding country
  roads and the racetrack. The tubular frame is made of welded steel
  tubes and forged components, with the parallel-twin engine integrated
  as a load-bearing element. Front wheel control via a KYB upside-down telescopic fork and
    rear wheel control via an aluminum hollow-cast double-sided swingarm
    with a KYB central spring strut.
At the front, a torsionally rigid 43 mm KYB upside-down
  telescopic fork controls the wheel. On the Sport suspension, the fork
  offers adjustable rebound and compression damping. At the rear, the wheel is guided by a closed, highly
  torsion-resistant yet lightweight hollow-cast aluminum double-sided
  swingarm. It is paired with a directly mounted KYB central spring
  strut with adjustable spring preload and rebound damping. Wheels and tires designed for dynamic riding pleasure.
The new BMW F 450 RR rides on lightweight yet robust
  cast-aluminum wheels. The supersport bike is fitted with tubeless
  tires measuring 110/70-17 at the front and 150/60-17 at the rear. Powerful braking system combined with BMW Motorrad ABS Pro for
    safe braking, even when leaned over. Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) and
    the dynamic brake light provide additional safety features.
At the front wheel of the new BMW F 450 RR, a floating
  single-disc brake with a Brembo four-piston monobloc fixed caliper and
  a 310 mm brake disc provides confident and efficient deceleration. At
  the rear, a single-disc brake with a floating ByBre single-piston
  caliper and a 240 mm disc is used. BMW Motorrad ABS Pro is standard on the new BMW F 450 RR. The system
  enables ABS-assisted braking when leaned over, increasing safety in
    corners. Dynamic Brake Control (DBC) enhances
  safety during braking in challenging situations by preventing
  unintended throttle application. The dynamic brake light effectively
  alerts following vehicles that the motorcycle ahead is slowing down. Sporty, active ergonomics and equipment for controlled,
    dynamic riding pleasure on winding country roads and the
      racetrack.
A carefully engineered ergonomic triangle and clip-on
  handlebars directly connected to the forged-aluminum triple clamp
  provide a sporty, dynamic riding position without losing sight of
  riding comfort. The bodywork and the 14-liter fuel tank beneath it are
  shaped for secure support and effective knee grip. The new BMW F 450 RR comes standard with a two-piece seat at a height
  of 790 mm, offering a balanced combination of comfort and a sporty,
  active seating position. Ergonomics can be customized with Original
  BMW Motorrad Accessories: the high Sport rider’s seat raises the
  seating position by 20 mm, while the low rider’s seat lowers it by
  15 mm. The gearshift lever, footbrake lever, and side stand are made
  of forged aluminum. The passenger footpeg brackets are bolted to the
  rear frame—an exceptional feature in this vehicle class. Reversible shift pattern for an extra dose of sportiness and a
    true racing feel.
For an extra dose of sportiness, the shift pattern can be
  reversed quickly and with minimal effort—ideal for racetrack use. Powerful LED headlight and LED lighting as standard.
    Connectivity with comprehensive information and functionality
    through a large, perfectly legible 6.5-inch TFT display. Practical
    USB-C port in the cockpit area.
The new BMW F 450 RR comes standard with an LED headlight
  featuring daytime running light LEDs and an iconic daytime running
  light signature inspired by the current generation of the S 1000 RR.
  The turn indicators and taillight of the new F 450 RR also use LED technology. The standard 6.5-inch TFT display on the new BMW F 450 RR offers a
  wide range of information, brilliant display quality, and intuitive
  operation at a premium level. The TFT display features the
  Pure Ride Screen. M Sport variants with Riding Modes Pro also offer
  three additional Sport screens with detailed information on DTC,
  braking force, and lean angle, as well as a lap timer function. Riders
  can also make phone calls, listen to music, and navigate conveniently
  while riding. Four attractive equipment variants for the new BMW F 450 RR. The new BMW F 450 RR is available in four equipment variants. The BMW F 450 RR Base is finished in Cosmic Black.
  Finished in Racing Red, the 
BMW F 450 RR Sport additionally features Shift
  Assistant Pro and the Sport suspension. The range-topping models are
    the BMW F 450 RR M Sport and the 
BMW F 450 RR M Sport with Innovation Package
  (including Easy Ride Clutch), in Snaefell white / M Motorsport,
  including Riding Modes Pro, Shift Assistant Pro, and the Sport
  suspension. Their white frame and rim stickers in M Motorsport colors
  create distinctive visual accents. Questions and Answers About the New BMW F 450 RR. The key questions about the new BMW F 450 RR—answered concisely with
  specific technical data. What is the BMW F 450 RR?
The BMW F 450 RR is a lightweight supersport bike for the
  48-hp class and the entry point into the world of BMW RR. It combines
  a 35 kW (48 hp) parallel-twin engine with supersport-specific chassis
  geometry, 17-inch wheels, and a ready-to-ride weight of 177 kg. It was
  developed for dynamic riding on winding country roads and for use on
  the racetrack. Who is the BMW F 450 RR designed for?
The BMW F 450 RR is aimed at riders looking for an accessible
  supersport bike with precise handling and moderate power. This
  includes A2 license holders as well as experienced motorcyclists who
  prefer a lightweight, direct motorcycle for winding country roads,
  everyday use, and their first or regular racetrack outings. Is the BMW F 450 RR suitable for an A2 license?
Yes. With 35 kW (48 hp), the BMW F 450 RR meets the maximum
  engine output permitted in Europe for the A2 license class. No
  subsequent power reduction is required. What distinguishes the BMW F 450 RR from the BMW F 450
  GS?The BMW F 450 RR uses the 420 cc parallel-twin engine
  familiar from the BMW F 450 GS, but is consistently tuned for
  supersport use. Key differences include chassis geometry, ergonomics,
  fairing, aerodynamics, 17-inch tires, and the sporty control strategy
  of the riding modes. The riding position is more front-wheel-oriented,
  and the shift pattern can be reversed for the racetrack. What are the output, torque, and weight of the BMW F 450
  RR?The parallel-twin engine produces 35 kW (48 hp) at 8,750
  rpm and develops maximum torque of 43 Nm at 6,750 rpm. As much as 80
  percent of maximum torque is already available at 3,000 rpm. The DIN
  ready-to-ride weight is 177 kg, or 178 kg with the Easy Ride Clutch. What is the effect of the parallel-twin engine’s 135-degree
    crankpin offset?
The 135-degree crankpin offset creates uneven firing
  intervals, shaping the engine’s power delivery and sound. Together
  with the counter-rotating balance shaft, this crankshaft design
  combines characterful power delivery with excellent refinement and low vibration. How does the Easy Ride Clutch on the BMW F 450 RR work?
The Easy Ride Clutch (ERC) uses a centrifugal unit that
  automatically engages the clutch according to engine speed. In
  combination with Shift Assistant Pro, the rider does not need to
  operate the clutch manually during regular riding. The clutch lever
  remains available for deliberate rider input. During overrun, the ERC
  stays closed, preserving engine braking until shortly before the
  motorcycle comes to a stop; at idle speed, it opens automatically and
  prevents the engine from stalling. Is the Easy Ride Clutch standard, and can it be
      retrofitted?
The Easy Ride Clutch is included on the BMW F 450 RR M Sport
  with Innovation Package. It is available for the other variants as a
  retrofittable Original BMW Motorrad Accessory. With ERC, the
  ready-to-ride weight increases by one kilogram to 178 kg. Which riding modes and assistance systems are standard?
The BMW F 450 RR comes standard with the “Rain,” “Road,” and
  “Race” riding modes. Standard equipment also includes BMW Motorrad ABS
  Pro for lean-angle-optimized braking, Dynamic Brake Control (DBC),
  Dynamic Traction Control (DTC), and engine drag torque control (MSR).
  Riding Modes Pro adds the individually configurable “Race Pro” riding mode. Is the BMW F 450 RR suitable for the racetrack?
Yes. The supersport-specific geometry, low weight, 17-inch
  tires, “Race” riding mode, and reversible shift pattern are designed
  for sporty riding, including racetrack use. The Sport variant and both
  M Sport variants also feature the Sport suspension, whose 43 mm KYB
  upside-down fork offers adjustable rebound and compression damping.
  Riding Modes Pro additionally provides “Race Pro,” Sport screens, and
  a lap timer function. How suitable is the BMW F 450 RR for everyday use?
Despite its supersport focus, the BMW F 450 RR is equipped
  for everyday use. Standard features include a two-piece seat at a
  height of 790 mm, heated grips, LED lighting, a 6.5-inch TFT display,
  connectivity, and a USB-C port. With a WMTC fuel consumption of 3.8
  liters per 100 km, the 14-liter fuel tank provides a calculated range
  of more than 350 km. Accessories such as a tank bag and soft cases
  expand its versatility for commuting and short trips. Is the BMW F 450 RR also suitable for shorter riders, and what
    seat height does it offer?
Yes. The standard seat height of 790 mm (31.1 in) already
  provides excellent accessibility. Through the BMW Motorrad Original
  Accessories range, the riding position can be adjusted by raising the
  seat height by 20 mm (0.8 in) with the Sport Rider’s Seat or lowering
  it by 15 mm (0.6 in) with the Low Seat. This results in an available seat height range from 775 mm to 810 mm
  (30.5 in to 31.9 in), allowing riders, particularly those of shorter
  stature, to tailor the ergonomics to their individual needs. Which equipment variants are available?
The BMW F 450 RR is offered in four variants: Base, Sport,
  M Sport, and M Sport with Innovation Package. The Sport variant adds
  Shift Assistant Pro and the Sport suspension. M Sport additionally
  offers Riding Modes Pro and the Snaefell white / M Motorsport color

title: Mending the fabric of your genes - HDBuzz
content: In plain language. Written by scientists.For the global HD community. Cells constantly mend tears and rips in the fabric of your DNA, like a cherished pair of jeans. Sometimes this mending can add C-A-Gs by mistake. A group of scientists examined whether other kinds of rips in the genetic fabric may be occurring in HD. Mending your genes is a bit like mending your jeans, with many different scuffs, rips, and loose threads in need of repair. Scientists know that a specific kind of DNA threading mistake causes the repeated C-A-Gs of HD to get longer and longer. But could other kinds of genetic mending also be involved in HD? A research group decided to assess a broad range of DNA repair activities in HD mice, to see what other kinds of genetic repairs might be happening. They showed that mending of double-stranded DNA breaks is increased in brains of HD mice and might contribute to  disease. The repeating genetic letters C-A-G are responsible for causing HD when someone inherits too many in a row in a gene called huntingtin. Over the past few years, major advances in HD research have shown that these problematic threads of repeating C-A-G can get longer and longer in some vulnerable neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information, through a process called somatic expansionsomatic expansion A process in which the CAG repeat in the Huntingtin gene can change over a person’s lifetime in some cells of the body, particularly in the brain.. By targeting somatic expansionsomatic expansion A process in which the CAG repeat in the Huntingtin gene can change over a person’s lifetime in some cells of the body, particularly in the brain., we might be able to preserve sick neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information and treat HD. However, scientists continue to debate how many repeated C-A-Gs cause a neuronneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information to get sick and lead to HD and whether all expansions are harmful. Your genetic code is packaged up as a double-strand of DNA in every cell of your body, like an extraordinary thread woven into genetic fabric. But as with any fabric, it can fray and develop holes over time. Fortunately, your body has many ways to spot damage to DNA and is equipped with a range of tools to repair it. Sometimes this damage is a partial break of only one DNA strand, called a single-strand break, like a frayed spot in your jeans where some threads remain. Other times the DNA double strand breaks completely, called a double-strand break, like a complete tear that leaves a hole. The DNA double strand can also be paired incorrectly, called a mismatch, like a thread that snags and pulls out. Your body is constantly mending these different kinds of DNA damage to keep the vital genetic fabric of your cells intact. In recent years, HD researchers have dug deeper on a surprising insight about how HD develops: those growing C-A-G repeats that can accumulate and eventually become toxic seem to happen as a byproduct of your body’s attempts to mend mismatched DNA. You read that right – C-A-G expansions can happen when the body is trying to repair slipped threads of DNA. While the mending is normally beneficial, repairing a C-A-G thread can sometimes actually add a few extra C-A-Gs by accident, like a tailor adding too much thread. It is increasingly thought that this is how so many C-A-Gs accumulate and become toxic in neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information – through errors made in repairing mismatched C-A-G threads. Although scientists have found that DNA mismatch repair can cause extra C-A-Gs to accumulate, it’s not clear whether other kinds of DNA mending might also be involved in HD. Understanding which kinds of DNA mending are disrupted in HD is important for developing the right kinds of drugs to treat all aspects of the disease. That’s where a new study comes in: Drs. Aris Polyzos and Cynthia McMurray from the Berkeley National Laboratory decided to look at what other kinds of DNA repair might be involved in HD. They asked whether double-strand breaks of DNA – clean cuts in the genetic fabric – are also a feature of the disease. Think of all the different kinds of tears and scuffs that your favorite pair of jeans might encounter. Mending each specific tear might require different stitching or technique. In the same way, your body has a suite of tailoring tools for all the different ways that your DNA fabric can fray and become damaged. Polyzos and colleagues looked at the brains of mice with HD to see how much these different kinds of DNA mending are happening. They found that the brains and neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information of HD mice have more mending associated with double stranded DNA breaks – a process distinct from mismatch repair. This raises an important question: does this mending of double-stranded DNA breaks happen in combination with accumulating C-A-Gs caused by mismatch repair, or does it happen independently? And might these double-stranded breaks be involved in HD? To try to answer this tricky question, the researchers looked at double-stranded DNA breaks in HD mice that have a lot of C-A-Gs but are engineered so that their cells are missing some of the machinery involved in mismatch repair. These mice engineered without mismatch repair don’t accumulate more C-A-Gs, since mismatch repair mistakes are how more C-A-Gs get added. Interestingly, in both the HD mice that accumulate more C-A-Gs and the mice that don’t, there were still more double-stranded DNA breaks than in healthy mice. These findings suggest that double-stranded breaks in the DNA fabric might be happening independently of mismatch repair and accumulating C-A-Gs. In these experiments, the authors showed that different types of DNA damage – double strand breaks and mismatch repair – can happen independently of one another in HD mice. This means that preventing extra double-stranded breaks in DNA of the brain might also be important for treating HD. There are still important questions about how these findings apply to people with HD. The researchers studied mice with far more CAG repeats than most people with HD inherit. At these very long repeat lengths, mice can develop disease-related changes even without further CAG expansion. This makes it difficult to establish whether DNA double-strand breaks contribute to HD in the same way in people, where CAG repeats typically start much shorter and can expand in some cells over many years. Further studies will be needed to determine whether these DNA breaks are a direct cause of neuronal damage in human HD, or one part of a more complex chain of events. Nonetheless, this research continues to expand our understanding of what goes wrong in neuronsneuron Brain cells that store and transmit information of people with HD – and how to mend it. title: Chairman and CEO David Solomon Joins CNBC from Our Builders and Innovators Summit - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. David Solomon discussed the firm’s third-quarter earnings, his outlook for near-term dealmaking activity, and continued confidence in the IPO market. He also shared his views on AI innovation, and the need for human and enterprise accountability and risk controls. Kelly Evans: Let’s begin with one of the standout bank names so far this earnings season. Increasingly so, as we see the raft of results today: Goldman Sachs. Yes, it’s down 2% in sympathy with other financials, but they reported their second-highest quarterly revenue ever yesterday. Earnings per share were $2 higher than the highest Wall Street estimates. Equities trading, investment banking, and wealth management all posting big year-over-year gains. Joining us now to weigh in on that, on what’s happening with AI financing, perhaps inflation, and so much else, Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon. And amid some speculation about his potential replacement, by the way, he’s out at Goldman’s Builders and Innovators Conference in San Francisco with that lady right there, Kate Rooney. Kate, over to you. Kate Rooney: Kelly, thank you so much. We are here with David Solomon. It’s great to see you in person. Thanks for having us. We’re at the Builders and Innovators Summit. You were just saying, 15 years now. Is this the 15th year? David Solomon: Well, first of all, Kate, thanks for being here. And this is a pretty great spot. It’s a nice place for you and I to have a day to be here and do this. But a little more than 15 years ago, we created this conference. The idea was to bring together really interesting entrepreneurs that were doing fascinating things and building interesting companies. I go back 15 years and I think about Travis Kalanick from Uber. I think about Dropbox. I think about Matthew Prince from Cloudflare. Drew Houston from Dropbox. These were some of the early entrepreneurs. They built great big companies. And here’s another class of 150 that are coming today. Some of these will be companies that, 10 years or 15 years from now, we’ll talk about. It’s been a fascinating place to see innovation and kind of the real engine of the U.S. economy and U.S. innovation. Kate Rooney: We want to get your take on the pipeline. It’s a great setup. But Kelly mentioned earnings. You guys are coming off one of your strongest earnings reports in the firm’s history. I wonder about durability, though. You talked on the analyst call about volatility helping you guys, this tech supercycle as you described it. What is the earnings engine going forward for Goldman if things start to change or rates really start to take a bite here? David Solomon: I think one of the things that’s missed in the narrative of day-to-day reporting and trading is that we’ve been working for eight years to really grow our franchise and increase the durability of our revenues and the diversity of our business. When we started eight years ago, we had a little less than $5 billion in management fees in our asset and wealth management business. We had $3.6 billion this quarter. We’re on a run rate of $15 billion in management fees. We have built now a firm where 45% of revenues are considered durable, recurring revenues. Now, of course, when you look at IPOs and M&A activity, there’s a little more cyclicality around those activities. But go look at M&A revenues for the last 15 years. Every year there’s M&A revenue, some years more than others. So we have a big, durable, diverse business in global banking and markets and asset and wealth management. And what we’ve done strategically as a firm is we’ve significantly lifted the floor of our business, both in terms of the revenue base and also the returns. I think investors are seeing that and rewarding that, and we feel very good about it. I can’t tell you what’s going to happen in the next three months or six months. I actually look out and see some very big equity deals coming. I see some potentially very big IPOs coming. I look at our M&A backlog. We said on the call yesterday our backlog is still at very, very robust levels. I feel very good about revenue accruals we have coming in M&A. I also see the strategic activity and dialogues that are going on, and I feel pretty good about it. Counter to that, we saw a slightly hot inflation print today. There are obviously four interest-rate hikes baked in. When you look forward, the 10-year Treasury has moved kind of 75 basis points in the last quarter and people are concerned about that. But we can operate in this environment pretty well, and we are operating well. We’ll just have to keep, quarter after quarter after quarter, showing people that our firm is a big, diverse, durable firm. Kate Rooney: Well, one of the things you said on the call was that 5% on the 10-year didn’t scare you. What is the number that would make you nervous? David Solomon: It’s all got to be put in context. But my point was, if you step back, the anomaly is the last 15 years after the financial crisis. David Solomon: Interest rates. That’s the anomaly. I mean, I’ve been around for 64 years. The anomaly is zero interest rates, not a 5% 10-year Treasury. Obviously, significant moves when they happen quickly upset markets and can have an impact. But you’re seeing the world absorb this move in the 10-year Treasury reasonably well. Now, if you continue to have pressure because of deficits, the fact that there is big demand for capital, I think one of the things that’s going on is there’s a lot of demand for capital for this AI cycle, and that’s also competing with the fact that governments have borrowed very aggressively. There’s a lot of demand for capital for government. So there is some pressure around that that affects rates. But I’m not scared about all this. This is the environment we live in and we operate in. Kate Rooney: Well, one of the things that is different, I mean, you look back 20 years and sure, rates were the same, but the amount of AI capex that is now reliant on debt is very different than what we’ve seen in the past. We had Broadcom’s CEO recently saying that he thinks capital could be the biggest constraint and really a potential choke point for this entire buildout. What do you make of that? David Solomon: I saw his comments. I have a different point of view. My point of view is there’s a lot of capital in the world. Think of the size of the market cap of public equities in the world. Think about all the savings that exist in the world. Think about the wealth that exists in the world. There’s a lot of wealth in the world. That doesn’t mean that everybody that has an idea, everybody that has a data center, everybody that has a chip, can have unlimited capital at a very, very low cost to pursue their aspirations. At the end of the day, capital is disciplined. It looks for returns. It goes to the best opportunities. I would just say there’s a lot of capital out there. The financing markets, particularly in this country, the capital markets are extraordinary and developing new ways to access capital and package capital. I think some of the things we’re talking about doing right now, and our partnership with NVIDIA around compute, are super interesting. Is there a crowding-out effect that at the margin affects the cost of capital a little bit? Absolutely. But that doesn’t mean the capital is not available. For good projects and good returns and good opportunities, there’s plenty of capital in the world. title: PTSC Marine GS, Pacifico Energy launch surveys for 1.8 GW offshore wind projects - Theinvestor
content:
Pacifico Energy Vietnam Co. and Vietnam Petroleum Technical Services Corporation (PTSC), through its PTSC Marine GS branch, on Tuesday launched survey work for two offshore wind power projects in Vietnam. Pacifico Energy Vietnam Co. is a member of U.S.-based Pacifico Energy Group, while PTSC is a subsidiary of state-owned Petrovietnam. The event marks a key step in Pacifico Energy's renewable energy development plans in Vietnam, moving from legal and regulatory procedures to actual offshore technical surveys. The launch ceremony was held at PTSC Marine GS headquarters in Rach Dua ward, Ho Chi Minh City. Pacifico Energy was represented by Pham Quoc Anh, executive chairman of Pacifico Energy Vietnam; Dhiraj Shangari, director of capital markets and investments at PE Group; and Nguyen Quynh Giang, general director of Pacifico Energy Vietnam. PTSC representatives included Le Chien Thang, deputy general director of the corporation, and Trinh Huu Duong, director of PTSC Marine GS, as well as executives from PTSC and PTSC Marine GS. In 2026, Pacifico Energy received approval from Vietnam's Ministry of Agriculture and Environment to use designated marine areas for surveys supporting two major offshore wind projects. The Southern offshore wind project has planned capacity of 500 MW, located in waters off Ho Chi Minh City. The South Central offshore wind project No. 3, located in waters off Lam Dong province, has planned capacity of 1,300 MW. With a combined planned capacity of 1.8 GW, the projects could attract more than $6 billion in investment in subsequent development phases, positioning Pacifico Energy among the foreign investors at the forefront of Vietnam's offshore wind sector. The survey campaign will begin with geophysical and meteorological-oceanographic surveys to collect data on seabed topography, geological characteristics and natural conditions. These studies are a crucial foundation for technical assessments, engineering design, and the overall development plans for the projects. Pacifico Energy's selection of PTSC, one of Vietnam's leading offshore engineering service providers, to undertake the initial survey package reflects a combination of international experience and domestic technical expertise and offshore infrastructure. The partnership also offers opportunities for Vietnamese companies to participate more deeply in the offshore wind supply chain, spanning surveys, port logistics, mechanical fabrication, construction and operations. Speaking at the event, Pham Quoc Anh, executive chairman of Pacifico Energy Vietnam, said the launch of the technical survey campaign reaffirmed the group's long-term commitment to Vietnam. "We believe offshore wind can provide large-scale clean electricity while helping establish a new industry, create jobs and open up opportunities for Vietnamese businesses. Our partnership with PTSC is a concrete step towards realizing that vision," he said. Le Chien Thang, PTSC's deputy general director, said the corporation continued to strengthen its competitiveness by drawing on years of experience in offshore projects and upgrading its capabilities to meet the stringent standards of the renewable energy supply chain. The contract further affirmed PTSC's leading position in renewable energy services in Vietnam and the wider region, he said. Arati Shroff, acting U.S. consul general in Ho Chi Minh City, praised the cooperation between the two companies, describing it as a practical example of efforts to advance clean energy initiatives and contribute to the Vietnam-U.S. Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The survey launch came shortly after a September 23, 2026 meeting in New York between Vietnam's Party General Secretary and President To Lam and Nate Franklin, chairman and founder of Pacifico Energy Group. The rapid commencement of offshore technical activities underscores the group's determination to translate its investment commitments into concrete action. Goldman Sachs comes into this earnings season with the stock under pressure, down almost 20% over the past three months and slipping another 1.5% today, even after posting one of its strongest profit runs on record. The headline is simple: the bank is minting money, yet the share price is moving the other way. Quarterly earnings per share of about US$17 and a return on equity near 19% put Goldman Sachs firmly in high gear for an investment bank of its size. That disconnect between rich profitability and a softer share price is the expectation gap you need to focus on now. The upbeat story on Goldman Sachs is that it can shift from volatile trading swings toward steadier fee income, while AI and alternatives quietly pull margins higher. This quarter gives that idea hard proof. Management says more durable revenue streams now account for about 45% of year to date turnover, more than double since 2020. Asset and wealth management delivered record US$3.6b in management and other fees and US$4.1t in assets under supervision, with 35 straight quarters of net inflows. Alternatives are not just a talking point. Assets under management in that area are up to US$491b with US$122b raised this year and a full year target of about US$150b. AI also shows up in deal flow, from data center financing to Nvidia linked structures. That mix helped Goldman Sachs post roughly US$18 in underlying EPS and around 20% ROE, which is exactly what bullish investors wanted to see. Bears argue Goldman Sachs faces structural margin pressure from fee compression, fintech competition and regulation that could blunt this pivot to steadier revenues. The latest quarter only partly answers that concern. Record US$3.6b in management fees, 35 consecutive quarters of inflows and US$4.1t in assets under supervision clearly undercut the idea that asset and wealth management are stalling. Fee rates or cost to serve those clients are not disclosed in detail though, so there is no hard proof that margins in these businesses are widening. On expenses, the efficiency ratio improved year to date to 59.4%, yet non compensation costs climbed 30% year on year, supported by higher transaction related items and heavier tech spend. The share price, now down about 20% over 90 days even after strong EPS, suggests investors are still treating these structural risks as unresolved rather than fully disproved. title: LG Electronics expands AI cooling push with GS E&C, GRC - The Korea Herald
content:
Business LG Electronics expands AI cooling push with GS E&C, GRC LG Electronics is teaming up with GS E&C and US cooling specialist Green Revolution Cooling to develop standardized immersion-cooling systems for artificial intelligence data centers, expanding its push into next-generation cooling technologies. The three companies signed a memorandum of understanding Tuesday at GS E&C's headquarters in Seoul to develop integrated cooling solutions and test their suitability for commercial data centers. The signing ceremony was attended by LG Electronics Executive Vice President Oh Se-gi, head of its ES Research Lab; GS E&C Executive Vice President Cho Sung-han, head of its Future Technology Institute; and GRC Korea branch director Choi Dong-hoon. Immersion cooling involves submerging heat-generating components, such as graphics or central processing units, in a nonconductive liquid to dissipate heat. The technology is gaining attention as AI data centers require increasingly powerful and energy-efficient cooling systems. Unlike conventional cooling methods, immersion cooling requires close coordination between cooling equipment and data center infrastructure, including building structures, piping, electrical systems and maintenance facilities. Under the agreement, LG Electronics will provide cooling technologies and operational data to develop systems based on standardized designs. GS E&C will handle architectural design and operate a test bed to evaluate equipment placement, structural loads, piping and power connections. GRC will supply immersion tanks and control systems, drawing on installation and maintenance data to improve performance. The partnership will add immersion cooling to LG's existing air- and liquid-cooling portfolio, strengthening its ability to offer integrated solutions for AI data centers. LG's current lineup includes high-efficiency chillers and fan wall units for air cooling, as well as coolant distribution units and cold plates for liquid cooling. "We will continue developing high-performance, energy-efficient cooling solutions to gain an early lead in the rapidly growing AI data center cooling market," Oh said. N. On market structure, he noted Goldman has repeatedly adapted to technological change, citing electronification of equities as a precedent where the opportunity set ultimately expanded. He said tokenization is an important trend across asset classes, that Goldman supported the CLARITY Act for the market clarity it would provide, and that the firm is engaged with agencies providing rules in the absence of legislation. Goldman has invested in digital asset market infrastructure for years, built its own digital asset rails (GSDAP), tokenized bonds and money market funds, and participated in the July launch of DTCC's tokenization service. He stressed current activity is very small and at the margin, but that the technology could drive efficiency, automation, lower costs and better liquidity over time. Q: Glenn Schorr and later Mike Mayo asked David Solomon directly about press reports of an accelerated succession process and his plans as CEO.A: Solomon said the articles "create noise" and stated plainly: "There is no succession transition or timeline underway at Goldman Sachs." He said he is pleased with the firm's progress since Investor Day, is "really enjoying the job," and that he and the Board are singularly focused on growing the firm, growing earnings and serving clients. On prime and equities financing, he said there will be cyclicality when equity markets fall and leverage unwinds, but over three-to-five-year periods the business is fundamentally correlated to global GDP and market cap growth.
